rankedTechniques.technique: Keyed Client region with its own frame clock (one per pane or per room), props diffed in, animation via surface.every + setState-on-change
rankedTechniques.evidence: Engine contract: "The engine keeps the instance (its local state, its timers) across the plugin's redraws while a Client under this key stays in the tree" (claude-code.d.ts 2.1.293:1494-1495); props "a new value on a redraw reaches the running instance, its state kept" (:1509-1510). Working on the desktop in glowup (hooks/client/pet.tsx:47-62, key "glowup-pet" register.tsx:1181; test/petclient.test.ts:143-155 five ticks -> 0 redraws) and claude-agentpane (live.tsx:19-34 re-anchors time without resetting the animation step). Our confetti.tsx:49-66 already follows the pattern on the terminal.
rankedTechniques.appliesToOurCase: The only persistence the API promises across our $.state-triggered redraws. Catch: ClientElements = terminal table minus Client/Raster/Image (d.ts:1391-1399) so NO Svg inside; the office becomes text cells (emoji or half-block pixel art as glowup does: pets.ts:119-148). Desktop Client is hedged in the typings ("desktop once it has them", :13913) and nothing on this machine has yet proven a Client mounts on the desktop (HANDOFF: no ui.fault hook, no fault line).

rankedTechniques.technique: Write $.state only when something drawn changed; keep timestamps/'now'/'tick' out of the atoms the pane reads; one atom per reader
rankedTechniques.evidence: agent-office register.tsx:136-142 change() + state.ts:225-231 sameWorkers (ignores changedAt), README:87; agent-watch register.tsx:426-438 (deep compare, updater returns the same object); agentpane register.tsx:470 JSON compare; glowup publishPet register.tsx:311-318 "a 1 s tick costs the pane nothing"; pixel-office sync.ts:242-252 structural vs detail signatures.
rankedTechniques.appliesToOurCase: We already have renderKey + CALM/SETTLE (register.tsx:295-306) but still pay extra full redraws for the retitle $.ui.open (register.tsx:324-332, diag lines 23-26) and finishBeat's deferred view write (ui.tsx:644-648, diag 29-32). Also HANDOFF.md:50/73 claim the desktop redraws on EVERY write of the mod, contradicting the documented readers-only rule (d.ts:3353-3355) ג€” must be re-measured, it decides whether per-reader atoms help at all.

rankedTechniques.technique: Single redraw funnel with a latch/debounce (100-150 ms) and no invalidate from write sites; batch high-frequency events into a Map flushed on a timer
rankedTechniques.evidence: anthropics diff mod register.ts:200-214 + limits/timing/redraw-coalesce-ms.ts (=100) "keeping the pane under the engine's ten redraws a second", refresh-debounce-ms.ts (=150); agent-office pendingActivity/flushActivity 2 s (register.tsx:144-152, 382-384); pixel-office busy reentrancy guard (register.tsx:20,33-47).
rankedTechniques.appliesToOurCase: Fold retitle, view write and payload write into one publish per poll; keep LIVE in module memory (already done, register.tsx:203-209). Halves the blink count immediately regardless of the element choice.

rankedTechniques.technique: Own the scroll window: hook ui.scroll for the pane's requestId, move your own offset, return {} without next(), draw only the rows in view
rankedTechniques.evidence: anthropics diff mod register.ts:878-897 + views/body/draw-window.tsx:27-104 (windowed with SCROLL_MARGIN_ROWS=8), README diff:7-9 "keeps the engine's window still"; glowup register.tsx:1221-1231 "No next(): the pane draws its own window, and the engine moving the whole body would carry the pet and status box off"; engine d.ts:4017-4018.
rankedTechniques.appliesToOurCase: A wheel tick then never changes e.props.scroll.offset (an input that re-keys the evaluation) and only the visible rooms are rebuilt; but the hook still invalidates, so with interactive Svg the blink is reduced, not removed. Pairs best with a Client (nothing to rebuild) or still images.

rankedTechniques.technique: Derive animation phase from the wall clock / deterministic offsets so a rebuilt frame resumes mid-cycle instead of restarting
rankedTechniques.evidence: pixel-agents register.tsx:70 frame=floor(now/200) "extra redraws cannot restart animations"; agents-panel drawing.ts:96-113 periods that divide the 1 s tick (but 1.6 s and 2 s slip); agent-office scene.ts:179 negative begin=(index*0.23)%1; agent-crew phase(id) stagger; glowup motion.ts:219-226 frame-seeded randomness.
rankedTechniques.appliesToOurCase: If any interactive Svg stays, compute `animation-delay: -((now % period))` per keyframe at render time so the reload is invisible except for the one-frame blank; this does not fix the blank itself (frame teardown) or swallowed presses.

rankedTechniques.technique: Non-interactive Svg (still image) for the picture, every clickable control as a keyed Button beside/under it

approaches.name: A. Client office: one Client surface module per room (text-cell characters, own frame clock, clicks inside)
approaches.summary: Desktop branch of ui.tsx replaces each room's `<Svg isInteractive>` rows with `<Client key={`room:${sessionId}`} module="./office-client.tsx" props={slimRoomProps} width="100%">`. The module draws a grid of tiles from Box/Text/Button only: emoji head or glowup-style half-block (ג–€ג–„) pixel sprite with color/backgroundColor, name, model pill, activity, mm:ss timer, badges; starts `surface.every(150-250)` once while state is undefined and calls setState only when a look signature changes; a plain Button per tile (or surface.onPointer) posts `{open:id}` / `{pin:sid}` and a new `on('ui.message', {module:'./office-client.tsx'})` hook in register.tsx writes view/prefs; optionally the hook answers `{ props }` so tiles update without any pane redraw. Hooks keep scanning, LIVE merge, renderKey (minus the per-minute terms), prefs/view, toast+audio, terminal cards, vscode/mobile Svg path, messageSvg.
pros: The only path with a documented persistence guarantee across the plugin's redraws (instance, state, timers kept while the key stays; d.ts:1494-1495) and a documented no-redraw push channel ({ props } on ui.message, d.ts:13946-13948)
Click on the character itself (surface.onPointer with capture, or a Button inside the region) with no dependency on the pane's redraw cycle
Animation and second-level timers cost zero $.state writes and zero engine publishes; a 750 KB payload change no longer touches the picture
One region per room instead of 5-100 sandboxed iframes each running CSS filters: likely far cheaper on CPU
Same tree works on the terminal (half-block sprites are the terminal's idiom too), so one module can replace both the text cards and the SVG office if wanted
Proven pattern in two community mods (glowup pet on terminal+desktop, agentpane live lines on all surfaces) and in our own confetti.tsx
cons: No Svg inside a Client (ClientElements = Box/Text/Button/Input/Select/Link/Code/Markdown, d.ts:1391-1399): the vector character, <title> tooltips and CSS keyframes are lost; the office becomes emoji/half-block cell art at the app's fixed code-font size (HANDOFF.md:39)
Desktop Text is LTR-only and bidi marks are refused (HANDOFF.md:52): Hebrew labels inside tiles only via row-reverse layout
vscode and mobile tables lack Client (d.ts:3824-3828) so office-svg.ts must stay for them or they fall back to text cards
Props must be rebuilt as slim JSON per room (<100,000 chars) and content-signed; the module runs under a 1 s per-call budget with tree bounds 20,000 nodes / 32 deep / 100,000 chars or it unmounts
Largest rewrite of the desktop tests (ui.test.ts Svg assertions :353-495, :621-733, :836-934 -> ui.find Client + ui.advance/ui.post)
risks: Client on the desktop is hedged in the typings ("desktop once it has them", d.ts:13913; "the desktop's alone today" vs the editor) and nothing on this machine has shown one mounting: if the app re-mounts the region on every pane redraw (HANDOFF.md:57 saw even a Text-only pane blink) the approach buys nothing
Unknown desktop cell metrics and styling: emoji width, whether backgroundColor/bold/dimColor and Box borders paint inside the region, whether width/height are honoured (d.ts:1513-1528)
Frame-clock cadence on the remote surface unknown; a 150 ms tick with 100 tiles could trip the 1 s per-call budget or the 3-consecutive-setState render-loop unmount (d.ts:1554-1556)
A throw in the module unmounts it to a blank region (interface.md); must pre-validate props in the hook (glowup spinner.ts:54-63) and hook ui.fault
Visual regression versus the current look; user may reject cell art
mustVerifyLive: Probe 1 (half day, before any code): a 20-line Client (surface.every counter + one Button) drawn under e.surface === 'desktop' with an on('ui.fault') hook writing phase/reason to the diag file: does it mount and tick at all in build 2.1.293?

Probe 2: with the counter ticking, press a toolbar Button, write a $.state key the pane reads, invalidate once a second, and scroll the pane: the counter must neither flash nor reset while the Svg rooms beside it do
Probe 3: surface.onPointer delivers down/up with region-relative cells on the desktop; a Button drawn inside the module raises ui.press; onKey arrives after a click (Escape returns focus)
Probe 4: ui.message answered with { props } reaches the desktop instance and changes the drawing with no 'render pane' diag line

Probe 5: cell metrics and styling inside the region (surface.columns/rows for the pane width, emoji width, Text color/backgroundColor/bold, Box border/backgroundColor, explicit width/height); half-block sprite legibility at the app's font size
Probe 6: CPU in Task Manager of one Client region with ~100 tiles at 150 ms vs the current iframes; confirm no render-loop unmount and no 1 s overruns
approaches.effort: Half-day probe + 3-4 days: office-client.tsx 300-450 lines (tile layout, sprite table, signature, pointer/post), ui.tsx -60/+50, register.tsx +40 (ui.message, ui.fault, slim props), tests ~350 lines rewritten + new office-client.test.ts

approaches.name: B. Keep Svg, make it still: one non-interactive Svg image per room + keyed Buttons, with strict redraw discipline (text-only cards as the fallback variant)
approaches.summary: Drop isInteractive permanently (the current נ���/נ�–¼ still path, ui.tsx:916) so each room is a static image that a redraw does not reload as a frame; one Svg per room with explicit height rather than per row; keep motion only as state-change pictures (different pose per status, walk-in/hop drawn once as a different frame) or none; Buttons under/next to each room with stable keys and $.ui.focus after navigation. In the hooks: fold retitle and view writes into the single payload publish, split atoms per reader, debounce the publish 100-150 ms, optionally own ui.scroll with virtualized rooms. Variant B2: skip Svg on the desktop entirely and draw the same Box/Text/Button cards as the terminal (what agent-watch and agentpane do).
pros: Smallest change; everything exists already (still toggle, CALM/SETTLE, renderKey, numbered Buttons)
Keeps the vector look, dark/light theming and RTL text inside the SVG; vscode/mobile share the path
No sandboxed iframes at all: removes continuous CSS-filter compositing, the biggest unmeasured CPU cost on the desktop
Community precedent on the desktop: agents-panel, savvy-progress, agent-office all ship non-interactive or single Svgs plus sibling Buttons
cons: No continuous animation and no <title> tooltips; 'animated office' becomes 'status pictures'
An image swap on a redraw may still flash (unknown); HANDOFF.md:57 says even a Text-only pane blinked, so B2 is not guaranteed flicker-free either
Click still lands on a numbered Button beside the picture, not on the character
Residual one-blink-per-publish remains if the desktop rebuilds images on redraw; scrolling still redraws unless ui.scroll is owned
risks: The still toggle was never checked by eye (HANDOFF.md:76): if the desktop replaces -style nodes on each redraw the blink persists and the whole approach only trims frequency
The readers-only rule may not hold on the desktop (HANDOFF.md:50 vs d.ts:3353-3355), in which case per-reader atoms are pointless and only fewer writes help
User may consider a static office a regression from the Python page
mustVerifyLive: Turn the still toggle on with ~10 running agents and watch by eye across 10 publishes and 20 wheel ticks: does a non-interactive Svg flash on redraw?
Draw the terminal text cards on the desktop for one session (B2) and watch: does a pure Box/Text/Button pane blink on a $.state write? (re-tests HANDOFF.md:57 under the current build)
Write a $.state key the pane does NOT read and check the diag for a 'render pane' line (readers-only rule)
Does the desktop pane raise ui.scroll for a wheel over the body with origin.kind === 'person' and placement === 'dock', and does returning {} without next keep the window still?
Measure presses on the numbered Buttons during continuous publishes: are any swallowed?
approaches.effort: 1-1.5 days: ui.tsx (one Svg per room, fixed height, focus restore), register.tsx (fold retitle/view into one publish, 100 ms latch, optional ui.scroll), tests adjusted; plus the shared perf work

approaches.name: C. Hybrid: still Svg room background (non-interactive) + one Client strip per room for the moving and clickable parts
approaches.summary: Per room: a non-interactive Svg draws the static scene (floor, desks, room title in Hebrew with direction=rtl, walls, posters) once and changes only when the roster changes; below or over it a `<Client key={`room:${sid}`}>` strip draws the live row of characters (emoji/half-block heads, typing hands, timers, badges) on its own clock and takes the clicks (Button per tile / onPointer). The hooks publish only roster/structure changes to the Svg and slim live props to the Client, with { props } answers for activity updates. Layout: Svg height = cols/rows computed from bodyColumns; Client height = rows * tileRows.
pros: Keeps the vector look for everything that does not move, including RTL titles that a Client cannot draw
Motion, timers and clicks live where the engine keeps state (the Client), so the per-publish redraw rebuilds nothing animated
Svg source for the background is byte-identical for long stretches, so even a desktop that reloads images on redraw reloads a static picture rarely
Degrades gracefully: on vscode/mobile only the Svg part draws; if the Client faults (ui.fault) the room still shows its picture
cons: Two layouts must agree in cells vs pixels (Svg is CSS px, Client is code-font cells; RenderViewport d.ts:10318-10324): alignment of a character 'on' a desk drawn in the Svg is fragile across widths and fonts
Most complex of the four: both pipelines, both test suites, two prop shapes
Still no Svg character; the figures are cell art on top of a vector room, which may look inconsistent
Inherits every unknown of A plus the Svg image-swap unknown of B
risks: Visual seams: row heights, uneven spacing already seen between Svg rows on the desktop (HANDOFF.md:61) will be worse with a cell-based strip under each
If the desktop re-mounts Clients on redraw (A's risk) the approach collapses to B with extra code
Tooltips are gone from the Svg part unless isInteractive is kept for the background, which brings the frame reload back
mustVerifyLive: All of A's probes 1-6
B's still-Svg probe (does a non-interactive image flash on redraw)

Pixel/cell alignment: measure the desktop's cell advance and line height at the default font vs the Svg's drawn width for 3, 4, 6 columns; check a tile strip lines up under its desks at two pane widths
Height stability: does a room Box holding Svg + Client keep a constant height across redraws (no reflow jump)
approaches.effort: Half-day probe + 4-5 days: office-client.tsx (as A, ~350 lines), office-svg.ts refactor to a background-only roomSvg (~150 lines changed), ui.tsx layout glue, register.tsx ui.message/ui.fault, tests for both parts

approaches.name: D. Embed the Python web page in the app's browser pane (mod becomes launcher + optional data source)
approaches.summary: Run `python -m claude_theater` (port 7333) and open http://localhost:7333 in the desktop's browser pane via $.mcp.call('Claude_Browser','preview_start',{url}) from a person-typed /theater command (not from session.start, which auto-mode refused), with a permission rule for mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start. The page's in-place DOM reconciliation was already observed blink-free in that pane (HANDOFF.md:78). The mod shrinks to: command registration, spawning/health-checking the server ($.process.run or a user-started process), the AbovePrompt band, toast/ding, and the terminal text cards; the scanner can move out of the engine entirely (the Python server already scans) or the mod can read /api/agents via $.http.fetch for the band.
pros: Only route with proven flicker-free continuous animation on this machine, with the full feature set already built: CSS keyframes, drawer with task/result, RTL/i18n, search, keyboard, click on character, confetti, ding
Lifts the heavy scan out of the Claude Code engine process (the suspected slowdown) into a separate process that can be profiled and throttled independently
1-2 days instead of a rewrite; the 2032-line Python page needs no changes
Works regardless of how the desktop treats Svg or Client redraws
cons: Not a 'mod pane': a separate browser pane, separate process, port, and a permission prompt; survives neither a reboot nor the app restart without the server running
Depends on an MCP tool (Claude_Browser) whose availability and auto-mode behaviour are outside the mods API; $.mcp.call from a person-typed command is untested (HANDOFF.md:78)
The engine's $.http.fetch exists but $.process.run is documented for CLI use; spawning a long-lived server from the mod may be refused or killed with the session
Two codebases to keep in parity (Python page + mod band/terminal cards) unless the mod's scanner is dropped
Terminal users still get text cards only; vscode gets nothing new
risks: Permission/auto-mode refusal makes the open flow clumsy (user runs the server and opens the URL by hand)
A browser pane tab may be closed/replaced by other Claude browsing; no engine-managed lifecycle (focus, placement, close hooks)
The Python scanner has the same whole-file-read cost unless it is also fixed; the slowdown may simply move to another process
The earlier $.mcp.call refusal may be a policy, not a timing issue
